national_raw_news.title: 41 mins ago | National 130 India, Uzbekistan Elevate Ties to Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, Sign MoUs Across Various S...
national_raw_news.content: India and Uzbekistan today announced to elevate their mutual Strategic Partnership to Comprehensive Strategic Partnership level. The Central Asian country also agreed to establish a framework for long-term supply of uranium to India and discuss the sites of the mining for rare earth minerals. India and Uzbekistan today signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) in various sectors, including Mining, Ayurveda, Tourism, Economic and financial dialogue, Comprehensive and strategic partnership, Higher education and the environment. Both Countries agreed to set a target of 5 billion dollars of bilateral trade by 2030, which is 5 times the current trade. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also received the highest award of Uzbekistan for his great work and efforts towards the cooperation between the two countries. The “Oliy Darajali Do’stlik” Order is Uzbekistan’s Highest Award for Foreign Leaders. “Oliy Darajali Do’stlik” ordeni, the Order of Friendship of the Highest Degree, in English reads as “Friendship of the Highest Degree” or “the Dostlik Order of the highest degree.” The highest-degree order is reserved for heads of state and government and comparable international figures. Our correspondent reports that on the second day of his visit to the Central Asian country, Prime Minister Modi held a bilateral meeting with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan and both sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral relations. The talks focused on expanding cooperation in the areas of trade and investment, infrastructure, critical minerals, mining, defence and security, innovation, agriculture, pharmaceuticals, health, information technology, digital public infrastructure, including UPI and education, among others. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said both countries have zero tolerance against terrorism, extremism and separatism. Mr Modi said, the cooperation between the two countries will not be restricted to the capitals but will extend to city and state-level partnership. During his announcement, Prime Minister Modi said, both countries will work for cooperation in the field of sports and promotion of Hindi. A scholarship was also announced for this purpose. The two sides decided to elevate the bilateral ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, reflecting the growing depth and expanding scope of cooperation. Both leaders witnessed the exchange of several MoUs and agreements covering a wide range of areas, including mining, culture, education, tourism, ayurveda, among others. A Letter of Intent for the restoration and conservation of the Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Kara Tepa in Uzbekistan was also agreed upon

national_raw_news.title: 44 mins ago | International 59 Nepal Issues Fresh Flood Alert for Bhote Koshi River
national_raw_news.content: Nepal has issued fresh alert for flood in Bhote Koshi River. It has urged residents living along the river in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts to remain cautious. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) of Nepal has reported an increased flood flow in the river. The warning comes the death toll from flash floods that struck the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday rose to 781, with more bodies being recovered. NDRRMA said, 8,186 people have been evacuated so far from the affected districts, including 227 foreigners. Over 2,500 people are still missing following the disaster. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said 149 Indian nationals have been rescued so far in Nepal following the tragedy. In a social media post, Mr Jaiswal said contact was re-established with around 50 Indian nationals who were earlier uncontactable. The External Affairs Ministry said that 275 Indian nationals are reportedly missing and around 128 people of Indian origin, holding other nationalities also remain missing. India is continuously supporting the relief and rescue operation in the flash flood hit Himalyan Nation. India has provided 68.5 tonnes of relief materials to flood-hit Nepal and sent technical teams, forensic experts and equipment to assist in search and rescue operations. A fourth flight carrying 11 tonnes of relief assistance landed in Nepal today. The World Health Organisation (WHO) has released One hundred fifty thousand US dollars from the Emergency Fund to support urgent health and other needs of the communities impacted by the devastating flash floods in Nepal. The organization said the emergency funds will support immediate response priorities as WHO is committed to support Nepal through the response and recovery efforts.

national_raw_news.title: 45 mins ago | National 9 PM Modi warns of perils of drug abuse in Mann Ki Baat programme
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today shared his thoughts with the nation in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani. In his address, Prime Minister Modi strongly warned against the social perils of drug abuse. He highlighted that Nasha-Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ campaign for a drug-free youth and a drug-free India is gaining momentum, with people joining in large numbers. He stressed that drug addiction harms individuals, families and society, while appreciating those working to raise awareness and help people overcome addiction. The Prime Minister also championed women-led economic empowerment through the PM SVANidhi scheme with nearly 35 lakh females across the country using the scheme to expand their businesses. Mr Modi celebrated growing avenues for women in advanced fields like the space industry. Mr Modi highlighted Mission ShaktiSAT, under which around 12,000 girl students from 108 countries are learning satellite technology. He said, the second phase of the initiative was launched at Gautam Buddha University at Greater Noida in Uttar Pradesh earlier this month on National Space Day. Prime Minister Modi also praised groundbreaking grassroots innovations in agriculture and digital technology. He lauded innovative farmers across Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu who shifted to or integrated avocado cultivation. He explained how scientific farming and direct marketing significantly boost rural incomes. He lauded Mumbai-based tech innovator Krishna Seshadri for creating a unique website www.bharatrajya.com. The interactive platform allows users to explore historical dynasties and find out which ruler governed different parts of India in any given year. Mr Modi noted that in the coming days, India is set to celebrate several more significant festivals, urging people to embrace ‘Vocal for Local’ during the festive season.

national_raw_news.title: Fresh Heavy Rain Revives Flood Threat in Odisha 1 hour ago 49
national_raw_news.content: Fresh heavy rain is aggravating the flood situation in several parts of Odisha, with rivers in north Odisha rising again under the influence of a well-marked low-pressure area over the northwest Bay of Bengal. The Baitarani is once again swelling in Jajpur, raising fears of another flood in low-lying areas of Dasarathpur, even as many families are yet to recover from earlier inundation. IMD has warned of extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places in Odisha today and tomorrow, with red alerts in Balasore, Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj. In Odisha, the flood threat has resurfaced with the Baitarani River rising again in Jajpur district. At Akhuapada, the river stood at 17-point-82 metres at noon today, against the danger mark of 18-point-33 metres, and continues to rise. This has raised fears of another round of flooding in low-lying areas of Dasarathpur, which could face its seventh flood this season. The situation is particularly worrying as Dasarathpur has been affected by floods since the sixth of last month, while several embankment breaches remain vulnerable. The IMD says a well-marked low-pressure area over the northwest Bay of Bengal is bringing heavy to very heavy rain. Red warning has been issued for Balasore, Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj, while Jajpur and Bhadrak are under orange warning.
